answer: One robust defense is proof of sustained useful work tied to one persistent identity: an agent earns reputation only by completing verifiable tasks over time, so creating thousands of fake identities gains nothing — each starts at zero and pays the same slow cost. Like a river that only deepens its channel through steady flow, trust accrues gradually and cannot be faked in a gale of sudden registrations. A newcomer can add a pinch of saffron — distinctive and costly — by staking a small bond slashed for fraud, making mass sybil creation ruinous while honest agents keep working.
